key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks provided strong shared-learning performance across related welding outputs.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between a shared multi-output model and a task-specific ensemble when estimating joint quality metrics for process optimization and quality control.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers + task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning
Predicted three welding responses: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness
Evaluated both methods using RMSE and R² on the same dataset
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower errors and higher R² overall (UTS RMSE 0.0263, R² 0.9863; weld hardness RMSE 0.0467, R² 0.9782; HAZ hardness RMSE 0.1109, R² 0.8453) than MTNN.
watch_item: The better-performing stacking model may be more task-specific and less robust when data are scarce or operating conditions shift, so external validation is important.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
